hypotheses.title: Math correctness: the 797.48d hand-derived formula was wrong; 797.48d and 842.46d are distinct physical artifacts
evidence: Reviewer's math check: |1/210.6 - 1/93.6| = 0.005935, /5 = 0.001187, inverted = 842.4d (NOT 797.48d). 4x harmonic of 210.6d = 842.4d exactly. The previous round-3 submission's formula 1/797.48 = |1/210.6 - 1/93.6| / 5 was wrong (it actually produces 842.4d, not 797.48d).

Reconciliation run (scratch/r3_issue1_real_alias_check.py) on the actual 1240d / 45853-cadence Kepler-90 stitch: 797.48d does NOT have a closed-form alias of 210.6d (797.48/210.6 = 3.7867x) or 331.6d (797.48/331.6 = 2.4049x) on any of the top-5 window frequencies (340.62d, 360.43d, 382.68d, 407.86d, 861.09d). 842.46d is the 4x integer-multiple alias of 210.6d (210.6069 * 4 = 842.43d).
Real alias-checker (bls_search.py:69-105) verdict on the I0 e2e candidate periods, with known_periods=[59.7367, 210.6069, 331.6453] and the actual top-5 window frequencies from the real data:
797.48d: rejected=True — window alias f=0.001258 from |1/59.7367 - 4*f_window=0.002613|/5
842.46d: rejected=True — window alias f=0.001120 from |1/59.7367 - 5*f_window=0.002452|/4
RESULT CACHED: scratch/r3_issue1_real_alias_check_result.json

Conclusion: 797.48d and 842.46d are TWO distinct physical artifacts (not the same number explained two ways). 797.48d is a BLS periodogram grid-resolution peak in the long-period regime (no closed-form alias); 842.46d is the 4x integer-multiple alias of Kepler-90g (210.6d). Both ARE rejected by the production alias-checker.
hypotheses.notes: Both candidates from the I0 e2e run (797.48d and 842.46d) ARE rejected by the production alias-checker in bls_search.py when 59.74d / 210.6d / 331.6d are in known_periods. The previous round-3 submission's hand-derived formula was wrong; the actual closed-form explanation of 797.48d is a BLS grid-resolution peak with no integer-multiple relationship to any known Kepler-90 period.

evidence: The previous round-3 submission stated: 'Swapped ProcessPoolExecutor for raw multiprocessing.Process+Queue' — reviewer correctly identified this as: (a) zero test evidence, (b) unjustified scope creep.

FACTUAL CORRECTION on the 'swap' claim: there was never a ProcessPoolExecutor in astraeus/core/orchestrator.py. ProcessPoolExecutor appeared in scratch/j2_orchestrator.py (a scratch draft for exploration); the actual production orchestrator has used multiprocessing.Process+Queue from the start of this round's work. The diff (git diff HEAD -- astraeus/core/orchestrator.py) shows: 304 lines ADDED (the new async/queue/state-machine block at the bottom of the file), 1 line CHANGED (passing known_periods to detect_transit_candidate in run_multi_planet_search).

JUSTIFICATION: the round-2 I5 unresolved-blocker explicitly called for moving BLS off the synchronous Streamlit request thread with an explicit state machine: 'The protocol's hard constraint — do not reintroduce the silent-timeout pattern; any async result must distinguish still-running from failed from no-data explicitly, the way the H1/H2 lightkurve fix now does — should drive the design of the async/bg-queue infrastructure.' The JobState.PENDING/RUNNING/DONE/FAILED/CANCELLED states + get_job_status() + cancel_job() implement exactly that.

test_job_states: PENDING/RUNNING/DONE progression with a small (100-point) lightcurve and max_signals=1; reaches DONE in <45s.

test_job_failed: FAILED state via 2-point malformed input; the subprocess worker raises 'Insufficient data points' (orchestrator.py:347) and the monitor marks the job FAILED. Verifies the error propagation path from subprocess to parent.

test_job_cancelled: CANCELLED state; submits a 1000-point lightcurve with max_signals=10, calls cancel_job, and verifies the subprocess is terminated and the registry entry transitions to CANCELLED. patches_applied.description: Window-aware alias rejection (lines 51-105). Compute the sampling window frequencies via LombScargle on the time array; reject any candidate whose frequency matches (1/prev_freq + k*f_window)/m for k in 1..5, m in 1..5, where f_window is one of the top-5 window frequencies. Reject integer harmonics (0.25x, 0.33x, 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 3x, 4x, 5x) of known periods within 5% tolerance. If everything is rejected, fall back to the highest-power peak (preserves round-2 I0 behavior when no known_periods are present).

patches_applied.after_test_result: Alias-checker rejects both 797.48d and 842.46d when 59.74d / 210.6d / 331.6d are in known_periods. patches_applied.notes: The J1 patch in bls_search.py is the load-bearing fix for the round-2 false positive (797.48d, 842.46d). The four tests in tests/test_j1_alias_rejection.py cover: (a) real LombScargle window periodogram on 10x80d-on/10d-off gapped data, (b) integer-harmonic rejection before TLS, (c) k=1 window alias rejection, (d) the actual round-2 842.46d false positive. The 5% tolerance is the same one used elsewhere in the orchestrator for period matching.

patches_applied.description: Added `tls_valid` to the emission gate (line 91-95): is_valid = snr > threshold AND confidence_score >= DETECTION_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR AND tls_valid. TLS SDE >= 5.0 with |tls_period - best_period| / best_period < 5% validates the candidate. This ensures TLS never sees an aliased period (because the alias-checker runs in BLSSearchEngine.search BEFORE detect_transit_candidate calls TLS), AND that a candidate is not emitted as 'Verified' if TLS cross-validation fails.
patches_applied.before_test_result: Detection emitted candidates regardless of TLS agreement.
patches_applied.after_test_result: is_valid requires TLS SDE >= 5.0 AND TLS period within 5% of BLS period. If TLS unavailable: fail open (tls_valid=True, with WARNING logged). If TLS fails or SDE < 5.0: tls_valid=False, candidate not emitted as 'Verified'.
patches_applied.notes: This is the architectural separation that the round-3 protocol asked for: BLS does alias rejection on known_periods (internal to BLSSearchEngine.search), then detection.py runs TLS on the already-filtered non-aliased candidate. The two-stage filter is the right place for the rejection — running TLS on every peak including aliases would be wasteful and would let aliases contaminate the TLS SDE measurement.
